Welcome from the Headteacher
As Headteacher, I’m incredibly proud to extend a warm greeting to you and your family. We are a school truly on the rise, deeply committed to every student’s success, and it’s an exciting time to be part of our community.At King’s Academy Brune Park, we firmly believe in the power of inclusivity. We are a highly inclusive school, where every student is valued, supported, and encouraged to reach their full potential, regardless of their background, abilities, or aspirations. We celebrate diversity and work tirelessly to create an environment where everyone feels they belong and can thrive.Welcome to King’s Academy Brune Park!
Our Journey of Improvement
King’s Academy Brune Park is on a determined journey of rapid improvement, resolutely focused on achieving excellence in all aspects of school life. This unwavering commitment means we are dedicated to:

Educational Visits
Learning Outside the Classroom – Trips and Visits
King’s Academy Brune Park offers a variety of Learning Outside the Classroom (LOtC) opportunities in the form of activities around the school grounds and off-site visits in the local learning area or further afield. All of which aim to supplement and enhance the curriculum or a chance to perhaps learn a new skill or to boost their health and well-being.
For any trip queries or financial support enquiries, please contact tripsandvisits@kgabrunepark.uk in the first instance.
All trip invite letters go out electronically via email. Those eligible will receive an invite from evolve.bruneparkvisits@edufocus.co.uk so please ensure you keep the school up-to-date with any changes to your contact details. Eligibility varies from trip to trip. These emails will give you the details of the trip and how to register your child’s interest. Copies of trip letters can be found below. No communication has been sent home for the provisional trips shown below.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
The Pupil Premium is additional funding for publicly funded schools in England to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils (those receiving FSM, CiC, or recently adopted).
The Pupil Premium funding is provided to schools which is in addition to main school funding. It is for schools to decide how the Pupil Premium is spent since they are best placed to assess what additional provision should be made for the individual students within their responsibility. The school’s Board has been kept closely informed over how the school uses the money.
To check if your child is eligible for free school meals, and to sign up if you are, click here and click on ‘I would like to check for free school meal eligibility’. You will be asked to input your national insurance number and date of birth. This is an easy online service that will give you a quick answer to see if your child is eligible.
To ensure the school is allocating Pupil Premium to aid the attainment of our students, we are rigorous in our approach and:
As a working document, our Pupil Premium strategy is updated termly in light of measuring implementation and spending in order to maximise impact.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
King’s Academy Brune Park is committed to securing improvement through developing and embedding an inclusive culture within which all learners, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), can be valued equally, treated with respect and provided with the opportunities and experiences to ensure they thrive and are successful.
The SEND Code of Practice (2014) considers a young person to have SEND if they have a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special education provision to be made. This may be due to the pupil showing a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others the same age, or having a disability which prevents or hinders him or her from making use of the facilities that are generally provided for others of the same age.
Identification of SEND
The needs of learners with a Special Educational Need or Disability (SEND) fall into four broad areas of need:
At King’s Academy Brune Park, learners are identified as having SEND via a variety of strategies including:
We use a wide range of tools, which form our Diagnostic Hub, to determine specific barriers to learning, including academic, emotional well-being, how connected the young person feels to their own educational setting and their self-view. This ensures an evidenced informed approach is consistently used when planning the most appropriate provision for a learner.
Communication and Interaction
Cognition and Learning
Social, Emotional and Mental Health difficulties
Sensory and / or Physical needs
Monitoring of progress within the curriculum
King’s Academy Brune Park Inclusion Leadership Team
Mrs RawlinsonMental Health Lead
Mr Millsjmills@kgabrunepark.ukInclusion Coordinator
Mrs MitchellChildren & FamiliesAlternative Provision
Who do I contact to discuss my child’s SEND?
you have a query related to the SEND or Inclusion needs of your child please contact:
Mr Mills will direct your query to the most appropriate member of the team and we will endeavour to respond to your enquiry as quickly as possible.
To help us meet the needs of every learner at King’s Academy Brune Park, we have a wide team of colleagues who work together, with students, parents and other professionals to identify SEND and arrange appropriate support and intervention. Colleagues from across the Inclusion Team, Year Teams, and Attendance Team work together to provide bespoke support that is matched to the individual needs of learners with a view to promoting independence, and maximising student achievement.
Support for Learners
Each learner on the SEND register will have a SEND plan created to detail the child’s individual strengths, areas of need and key supportive strategies to be implemented in lessons. Any supporting documents such as an Education and Health Care Plan (EHCP), outside professionals reports, or in school diagnostics are collated on our online inclusion database – Provision Map. This information is available to all staff who support the learner to inform them of how best to support the child in school. The majority of learners’ needs will be met through inclusive practice and high quality adaptive classroom teaching.
A number of interventions are also available to help young people with their particular barriers to learning. We run a wide range of interventions to address all four areas of need, for example:
Bespoke Reading Support and Intervention
Numbers Count and Numeracy Intervention
Zones of Regulation
Drawing and Talking
Pastoral, mentoring and well-being intervention
ELSA – Emotional Literacy Support
Life skills interventions

Curriculum Overview
At King’s Academy Brune Park we have a curriculum that is ambitious for learners, that is rooted in knowledge acquisition and skill development. Teaching and learning is led by the needs of the learner.The curriculum is broad and balanced, with the aim to allow all learners to progress and achieve well, preparing them for key stage transitions, end-of-school assessments, and life beyond King’s Academy Brune Park empowering them to compete in a global community. Mapping and sequences of learning are reviewed and adapted regularly by subject leads to consider how further progress can be facilitated. The curriculum allows students to build key knowledge over time, we develop opportunities for memory recall in lessons, allow students to activate, apply and remember their learning using a range of teaching and learning strategies.
All learners have a full dynamic curriculum offer where there are adaptations to meet SEND and inclusion needs.If you require additional information about the curriculum please contact Mr Irving – jirving@kgabrunepark.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values – King's Academy Brune Park
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Our school strives to be a beacon of inclusive excellence, where every student feels valued, supported, and inspired to achieve their full potential. We are committed to fostering a positive, aspirational environment that celebrates diversity, encourages curiosity, and promotes growth.
Every student has the right to feel safe, happy, and authentically themselves, irrespective of their background, race, religion, or identity. We champion equality, diversity, and respect for all, embracing the individuality of each student while striving for academic excellence. We aim to equip our students with a global outlook, fostering an understanding of the wider world and encouraging the development of character, curiosity, and cultural awareness. By connecting with communities locally and globally, we provide learners with opportunities to broaden their horizons and build meaningful connections.
At King’s Academy Brune Park, we work closely with families, creating a supportive partnership that values their involvement in shaping education. Together, we are building a rapidly improving school that equips our students with the skills, resilience, and confidence to thrive in an ever-evolving world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Join Us in Supporting Our School’s Second-Hand Uniform Shop! – King's Academy Brune Park
pageCache.text:
We’re excited to announce the launch of our new Second-Hand Uniform Shop at King’s Academy Brune Park! As part of our commitment to providing affordable options and reducing waste, we invite you to contribute to this initiative by donating any outgrown school uniforms.
With your support, we can ensure that every piece of clothing finds a new home, benefiting both our families and the environment. You can drop off uniform to reception now and Miss Ringland will be coordinating making it available during the summer break.
Your contributions will directly support our efforts to support sustainability within our school community.
Thank you for your generosity and ongoing support. Together, we can make a difference!
